commit.message:
Support OpenAI-compatible LLM APIs alongside Claude

All three AI routes now go through src/lib/server/llm.ts, which sends one
system prompt + one message and checks the JSON reply against a zod
schema. It speaks two API formats, chosen in .env.local:

- LLM_API_FORMAT: anthropic (Messages API, default) or openai-chat
  (Chat Completions, which most other vendors and local servers speak)
- LLM_API_KEY / LLM_BASE_URL / LLM_MODEL: one set of names whichever
  vendor you use; the official URL gets a cheap default model
  (claude-sonnet-5, or gpt-6-luna at low reasoning)
- LLM_EFFORT: unset sends no reasoning params, the cheapest option and
  one every model accepts
- LLM_JSON_MODE=object: for vendors without json_schema support

Replaces ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and claude.ts. A reply that isn't valid JSON
or doesn't match the schema becomes the routes' normal 502.

Read a finished piece: count the stitches in a photo of crochet

The stitch grid is found from the photograph itself: a comb laid on how hard the
image bends along each axis, scored as a significance statistic so a true count
beats a lucky handful and a doubled or tripled one. Width and height are counted
separately, each stitch's colour is the median of its middle, near-twin yarns are
merged, and the piece's width in centimetres turns the same photo into a tension
measurement. Also: a layout guide (rings, thirds) no longer drives the basket
lookahead, only a guide whose yarns you hold does.

chore(bench): replay real sessions to price what terse did to billed cost (#502)

## What

`scripts/bench/replay_sessions.py`: an offline analysis that prices
terse's effect on billed cost in real Claude Code sessions, from the
ledger and the transcripts already on disk. No model calls. 48 unit
tests in `scripts/bench/tests/`.

## Why

The pre-registered cost-per-task suite is short single-question tasks
(median 2 calls, 3-4 tools allowed, secret-broker excluded). It
over-weights the one-time primer and cannot show a smaller result being
re-read on every later call. It stays as a regression check; this is the
value measurement.

## How

1. Group ledger rows into results and join each to a transcript tool
result: same tool, nearest timestamp at or before, sizes must agree. A
group that is really parallel calls is split into rows. Pairings that
disagree are dropped and counted.
2. delta = raw minus what the model was shown, tokenized from the
transcript, so the primer is charged to terse.
3. Price delta on each later API call from that call's own usage: write
rate on first carry, read rate after, write rate on a cache rebuild,
nothing after compaction. History copied into a resumed session is
billed once.
4. Charge each `terse_retrieve` its result tokens plus the cached prefix
its extra call re-read.
5. Scale cl100k to billed tokens by a per-model ratio measured from the
transcripts.

The run stops before pricing if under 90% of the results terse changed,
or of the saved tokens they hold, join.

## First run (2026-10-06, maintainer's data, 6,726 transcripts)

- Join: 2,547 of 2,649 changed results (96.1%), holding 96.7% of the
ledger's wire saving. All results: 89.7%.
- Net: +31.8M input-equivalent tokens = 0.58% of all scanned sessions'
cost.
- Sessions that carried a terse result: Opus 5.5 +1.66% (71), Sonnet 5
+1.25% (144), Opus 5 +0.97% (208), Haiku 4.5 -5.01% (19 short sessions).
- 90% of the net is in sessions over 100 calls; sessions of 1-5 calls
lose slightly.
- `secret.list_credentials` is 75% of the net. The codegraph drop is
8.6M gross, with retrieves costing 3.9M.
- Untouched results sum to a delta of 3 tokens against 935,429 shown.

## Limits

- Assumes the model would have made the same calls with terse off. Task
success is not observable.
- The join gate was changed after the first run stopped at 83.3% of all
results: it now tests changed results and saved tokens. The overall rate
is still printed.
- 26 results terse kept inline that the raw path would have offloaded
count as zero; the pessimistic bound is -7.5M.
- 15 dropped pairings look like primer-carrying results, an uncounted
cost.
- Not charged: a primer sent at `initialize` by a router older than
#212, the retrieve tool definition, a retrieve call's own output tokens.

## Verification

```
uv run python -m pytest -q        2933 passed in 250.79s
uv run ruff check .               All checks passed!
uv run mypy                       Success: no issues found in 32 source files
```

The script had four review passes before it priced anything; each
finding is pinned by a test. No change under `src/terse`.

commit.message:
Enforce CSRF on admin writes by authenticating the session cookie ourselves

Spring's oauth2ResourceServer skips the CSRF check for every request that
carries a bearer token. Our token is read from a cookie the browser sends
on its own, so admin POST/PUT/DELETE passed without any X-XSRF-TOKEN. Only
SameSite=Strict was left as protection.

A small CookieAuthenticationFilter now decodes the JWT cookie and sets the
authentication, so CsrfFilter keeps guarding all writes. Unauthenticated
requests still answer 401 through an explicit entry point. Regression tests
cover a valid session with a missing and with a wrong CSRF token, and an
invalid session cookie.

docs(skill): trigger the rbx-forge skill on Roblox work, not on forge (#143)

## Summary

The skill description now names the moments it changes, not the tool. An
agent no longer has to know the project uses forge before the skill
fires.

```diff
 description:
-  Dev loop for Roblox projects that use rbx-forge (`rbx-forge.config.ts`). Use
-  when implementing, testing, or debugging code in such a project, reading its
-  compile errors, or checking it in Roblox Studio.
+  Use before changing code, building, or using Roblox Studio in a Roblox
+  project, and when syncing Studio edits back.
```

One trigger per branch of the skill body: the loop (a code change), a
build check, Studio (snapshot or attach), and syncback. Setup needs no
trigger: a request to set up forge names the skill. 34 words → 21.

## Evidence

- **Before:** `claude -p` in a roblox-ts fixture with
`rbx-forge.config.ts`, 3 repeats each on Haiku, Sonnet, and Opus. The
old description loaded the skill on 9/9 compile, 9/9 Studio, and 9/9
syncback prompts, and on 0/9 control prompts (a general Roblox
question).
**After:** An earlier draft of the new description had the same result:
9/9, 9/9, 9/9, and 0/9.

Gap: the final wording in this PR is not tested. A harder run (an
implement prompt with no "compile" in it, a debug prompt, and a fixture
with no config file) was stopped before it finished.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Revert the commit to get the old description back.

**Blast Radius:** skill triggering

Agents in projects that install the skill (`npx skills add
christopher-buss/rbx-forge`). The skill now fires at the start of a code
change in any Roblox project, so it can load in a project that does not
use forge. Its Setup section covers that case. CLI behavior and `--json`
output do not change.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Split the gallery into Classic and New tag styles sections

Two collapsible sections: Classic tag styles (options below 22) and New tag styles (22 and up). Each is a wide header bar with a live sample tag centred between the title and a chevron. Both start collapsed; opening one builds its cards and slides them in from the left one at a time (70 ms stagger), closing just hides it with no animation, and re-renders from the companion or hearts toggles do not replay the animation. Cards are only built while their section is open, which also keeps the page light. Skill and README updated.
